title: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry: Chapter Introduction
summary: One drop of water holds about 1.7 × 10²¹ molecules. The chapter shows how chemists measure matter and count its particles with the mole.

notes.title: 00 – Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry: Chapter Introduction

keyPoints: **Lavoisier**: mass is neither created nor destroyed; such laws led **Dalton** to atoms.
**1 mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles**, a counting unit like a dozen; it powers **stoichiometry**.

sections.h: How many molecules in one drop?

blocks.p: A drop of water is about 0.05 g. Its molecules:
Counting one per second would take about 5 × 10¹³ years, far longer than the age of the universe (about 1.4 × 10¹⁰ years). So chemists count in moles.
